prompt: Wardrobe: Top: One solid muted cocoa-taupe sleeveless mock-neck crop top made from a fine-gauge stretch mesh knit with tightly regular micro-openings, a lightweight semi-sheer section, a smooth low-luster face, soft close drape, and resilient multidirectional recovery. Cut a close straight-to-lightly-tapered body ending at the upper waist, with matching front and rear lower-edge levels and minimal bulk. Form a narrow circular self-fabric mock neck whose finished height is between one-tenth and one-sixth of the shoulder-to-hem length, using a double-layer return and one low-bulk rear join. Continue two narrow shoulder sections into high-cut sleeveless armholes and uninterrupted front and rear body panels. Finish both armhole circuits with narrow self-fabric turned bindings less than one-tenth of the shoulder-section width, join the body through two clean side seams, and complete the lower circumference with one narrow straight double-turn hem. Use the knit recovery and complete neck opening for a pull-on construction without exterior fastening. Keep the mesh scale evenly legible, the semi-sheer density consistent, the mock neck softly upright, the armhole edges flat, and the lower hem free of heavy opaque bulk. Bottom: One camel-tan wrap-front mini skirt made from medium-weight brushed twill with a compact diagonal weave, a short soft nap, a matte low-luster surface, firm shape retention, and rounded low-bulk folds; confine espresso brown, ivory, and muted dusty-rose to the woven geometric check and matte black to two front buttons. Cut a high-rise upper-thigh mini length with a close waist and upper hip, then widen gently into a compact A-line hem whose laid-flat width is between one-and-one-fifth and one-and-two-fifths of the top-edge width. Form a clean curved faced upper edge without a separate exterior waistband. Build smooth front and rear bodies with two equal rear waist darts, one at product-right and one at product-left, two side seams, and one full-height product-left front overlap panel spanning between one-half and two-thirds of the front width; keep its vertical free edge straight from the top edge to the hem and its underlap continuous behind it. Cover every front, overlap, side, and rear panel with a woven repeat of large upright camel rectangles bounded by single espresso lines and paired ivory lines, then add one fine dusty-rose pinstripe only to alternating vertical and horizontal corridors so the rose intersections shift by one cell on every second row; each complete repeat spans between one-quarter and one-third of the laid-flat front width, with straight orthogonal lines and clean registration across darts, seams, and the overlap. Mount two circular matte-black four-hole buttons in one vertical product-left-front line, each between one-tenth and one-eighth of the waist-to-hem depth in diameter; place the upper station within the upper quarter of that depth and the lower station between one-half and two-thirds of the depth. Secure the overlap through two matching reinforced buttonholes on the underlap, keeping both stations fully engaged and the panel flat, and finish the complete lower edge with one narrow turned hem. Preserve the short brushed nap, readable diagonal weave, crisp A-line outline, stable overlap depth, aligned geometric repeat, flat button seating, and material-correct hem thickness. Footwear: One matching pair of predominantly black combat boots built from medium-thick semi-matte coated leather-like upper material with a fine shallow grain and broad flexible crease response, black flat woven cord, silver-tone metal, and deep black molded rubber. Each boot is knee-high with a tall straight shaft, a broad rounded toe, a substantial forefoot platform, and a slightly deeper rear block, with shaft volume remaining open and stable near the top before compressing into broad slouch folds through the lower shaft and ankle. A wide straight topline forms the shaft opening and retains a clean finished edge. The upper consists of tall side and rear shaft panels joined to a rounded forefoot, broad vamp, quarters, and a central tongue; the vamp stays close while the shaft carries relaxed vertical volume. Paired rows of black lace holes run from the forefoot into the lower shaft and hold flat black laces, while two separate narrow wrap straps encircle each boot, one near the upper shaft and one at the ankle, each ending at its own compact rectangular silver-tone buckle. Tonal topstitching defines the panel joins, and the sole forms a thick continuous sidewall above a deeply cut lugged contact face. The laces close in compact tied bows and both buckle straps remain fastened through their rectangular frames. Both boots are identical anatomical mirror counterparts with the same panel layout, lace path, strap count, buckle placement, shaft height, slouch distribution, toe shape, and sole stack. Preserve the coated fine grain through the broad folds, keep the two buckle circuits physically separate from the lace closure, and maintain crisp sole edges, deep lug relief, firm toe volume, and material-correct seam bulk. Bag: Styling — highest priority: - Bag carry: Hang the strap from the wearer-right shoulder only without crossing the chest, and let the bag body lie flat along the right flank between the lower ribs and outer hip. Let the strap bear the full weight and keep both hands off the bag and strap. Keep the complete strap and bag body entirely outside and visibly separate from every garment, routing the strap over, never beneath or through, the outermost clothing. Do not pass it through any neckline, sleeve, knit opening, seam, or rear panel, and do not merge, attach, weave, replace, or reinterpret any bag material as part of a garment. - Finish — Natural: Adjust only material-correct slack and body contact along the exact selected strap route. Keep the selected route and all attachment points exact while allowing limited material-correct slack and natural body contact. One warm-ivory soft gathered chain-strap pouch bag made from lightweight lightly padded matte woven fabric, constructed as one medium rounded crescent-like body with softly tapered upper corners, a broad curved lower edge, shallow expandable side depth, and controlled flexible volume. Gather the complete upper body into one reinforced top-edge opening, producing repeated soft vertical folds that release through the front, rear, and side surfaces without rigid quilting lines. Add one long warm-gold-tone curb-chain strap attached through two small polished gold-tone D-rings and reinforced matching fabric tabs at the upper sides, preserving identical attachment height and hardware construction on both ends. Complete the front, rear, side panels, curved base, gathered upper edge, reinforced top opening, chain strap, D-rings, attachment tabs, hidden seam allowances, and internal soft support as one coherent bag with no visible exterior closure hardware, exterior pocket, readable branding, detachable charm, keychain, plush ornament, mascot, or additional decoration. Preserve lightweight textile response, softly padded body volume, even gather distribution, clean upper-edge reinforcement, secure chain anchoring, low seam bulk, and restrained warm-gold reflections. Necklace: One short silver fine-chain necklace built as one continuous closed circuit with a shallow curved ornament centered on one product axis. Keep most of the circuit as a slender uniform chain and confine the ornament to a short lower arc substantially shorter than the complete chain path. Construct the ornament from a closely spaced row of uniform short rounded cylindrical beads aligned radially to form a gentle crescent, connecting both ornament terminals directly into compact polished chain links. Maintain bilateral orn
